case_name: Akhil Ali Jehangir Ali Sayyed v State of Maharashtra
respondent:
State of Maharashtra
Supreme Court of India

24 January 2002
Cr.A. No. 1123 of 2001
The Judgment was delivered by: Thomas, J.
1.  In this appeal, we passed an order even when special leave was granted that the consideration would be limited to the nature of offence. Appellant was the first accused. He was arraigned along with one Jabbar as second accused and another person as the third accused in a murder case. The trial court convicted all the three accused of the offence under Section 302 read with Section 34 for the murder of one Moulana Mohammed Yusuf Sheikh. The High Court acquitted the third accused but confirmed the conviction and sentence passed on the first and the second accused. We are told that the second accused preferred a special leave petition No. (2828 of 1999) before this Court and the same was dismissed. Subsequently, he filed a review petition which was also dismissed.
2.  This appeal by the first accused has to be considered only on

The High Court acquitted the third accused but confirmed the conviction and sentence passed on the first and the second accused.

One thing is apparently clear from the above dying declaration.
Ms. Neeru Vaid, learned counsel for the appellant then contended that the appellant had injuries on his person and that would show that he had not exceeded the right of private defence.
We are told that appellant has been in jail for nearly ten years by now.

As the second accused Jabbar was placed on the same situation as the appellant in this case (if not lesser), Article 21 of the Constitution would not permit us to deny the same benefit to the second accused, notwithstanding the fact that the SLP and the review application filed by him have been dismissed by this Court.
The following passage from the said decision can be profitably extracted below:

After bestowing our anxious consideration on the fact situation in this case and also the spirit of Article 21 of the Constitution, we hereby order that the conviction passed on the second accused Jabbar shall also stand altered to Section 304, part I and a sentence of rigorous imprisonment for ten years be awarded to him.

holding: The conviction passed on the first accused shall stand altered to Section 304, part I of the IPC.
The sentence awarded to the first accused is rigorous imprisonment for ten years.
The conviction passed on the second accused Jabbar shall also stand altered to Section 304, part I and a sentence of rigorous imprisonment for ten years be awarded to him.
